motion.name: ease-out-expo

motion.name: redline-sweep
motion.purpose: The rose wash sweeping in under a search match; removed under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: find-stroke
motion.purpose: The find row's 2px rose-ink focus stroke drawing left to right along its bottom rule; removed under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: fade
motion.purpose: The sheet in hand's tint and corner crosses fading in, link and sheet-title colour to rose-ink, and the find row's tint.

focus.offset: 1px; -2px (inside) on sheets, which also show their rose-ink corner crosses
focus.findRow: 2px rose-ink stroke along the bottom rule plus a 20% rose-wash tint; the input outline is suppressed

drawing.column: max 76rem; width calc(100% - 2rem), calc(100% - 4rem) from 640px; centred
drawing.rails: 1px rule, full height: the column's inline borders
drawing.rows: 1px rule top border across the full window width; the row under the nav rule and the 24px lead-in draw none
drawing.registrationMark: 11px cross of two 1px ink-3 strokes, centred on each rule/rail crossing
drawing.sheetMark: 11px rose-ink crosses centred on the four corners of the sheet under the pointer or focus
drawing.sharedEdges: cells draw right and bottom only; the grid is pulled 1px under the rail and the next rule
drawing.table: body and html are painted table; the column paints itself ground, so the table only shows in the margins
drawing.marginHatch: 1px rule lines at -45deg, 7px pitch, in a 28px band beside each rail, full page height in one piece; no knockout under crosses
drawing.constructionGrid: 1.5px ink-3 dots at 55% opacity on the 16px unit, measured from the rail; masked to rise from the lettering cell bottom-right (60% x 110% ellipse, 45% x 90% below 640px)

narrative.overview:
docs.osm.sh is a drafting workbench in daylight, and it belongs to the same osm.sh family as puzzles.osm.sh. Every surface is one ruled drawing on a single sheet of paper, laid on a drafting table. A column stands between two rails that run the full height of the page. Hairline rules cut it into rows and run the full width of the window, and a small registration cross sits wherever a rule crosses a rail. The labelled nav rule is the drawing's first rule. Under it, the knowledgebase's title block is the banner, the find row is the search, a ruler measures the drawing, and every page is a cell in the sheet grid below. Outside the rails the table shows through, hatched in a band beside each rail, and each title block's lettering cell carries a faint construction grid. The palette is a whiteprint: warm paper, navy text, `rule` hairlines, and rose redlines that mark what the search found and which sheet is in hand. Fira Code is the only face, corners are square, and nothing casts a shadow.

Search comes first. The caret waits in the find row on arrival (fine pointers only), `/` returns to it from anywhere, and typing narrows the sheet grid live while the matched words are redlined on every sheet that stays. The index does not sort sheets by kind. Writing, projects, and notes still exist as directories and URL segments (`/writing/…`, `/projects/…`, `/notes/…`), but on the index they are one numbered set, newest first. Sheet numbers count up from the oldest page as three-digit numbers (`001`), so the newest sheet carries the highest number. Opening a sheet draws it at full size between the same rails, with its own title block across the top, and `h` or `q` puts it back where it was.

An empty knowledgebase looks empty. With no pages the title block reads `0` sheets and `# none` for last rev, the find count reads `0 sheets`, the sheet row holds a single note, `# nothing published yet`, and there is no footer.
keyCharacteristics: One face, Fira Code, with ligatures off on a 16px base. Chrome weights are 400 and 500, and 700 appears only as `strong` inside prose.

Paper on a table. The column is `ground` paper. The margins outside the rails are the `table`, with a 28px band of 45° `rule` section hatching beside each rail. Inside the column there is no mat, panel, or card surface.
One line colour. Every rule, rail, and cell edge is a 1px `rule` hairline. Emphasis comes from marks, never from a heavier line.
Rules run edge to edge of the window, and content stays between the rails (at most 76rem).
Registration crosses in `ink-3` sit on every point where a rule crosses a rail. The sheet in hand gets `rose-ink` crosses at its four corners.
Rose is the redline: the search-match wash, the find row's focus stroke, the marks on the sheet in hand, focus rings, hovered links, and text selection.
The labelled hairline nav rule opens every surface and is part of the family system.

rules.name: The Redline Rule
rules.body: Rose marks a finding, a live focus, or the sheet in hand, and nothing else. The wash sits under matched words, the rose-ink stroke under the focused find row, and the rose-ink crosses on the corners of the sheet under the pointer or focus. Outside a match, rose's only fill is the find row's 20% wash while it holds focus.

rules.name: The Paper and Table Rule
rules.body: The drawing is `ground` paper lying on the `table`. Texture comes only from the drafting world, and it is drawn as linework: 45° section hatching (1px `rule`, 7px pitch, 28px wide) in the margins beside each rail, and the construction grid in a title block's lettering cell. There is no mat, panel, or card surface inside the column. `ground-2` appears only inside prose, in the scrollbar track, and as the tint of the sheet in hand.

rules.name: The One Line Rule
rules.body: Every line is a 1px `rule` hairline. No line darkens or thickens to show emphasis. Emphasis is a mark added to the drawing: an `ink-3` registration cross, a `rose-ink` corner cross, or the 2px `rose-ink` find stroke.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Fira Code is the only family, and inputs and buttons inherit it. KaTeX's math faces are the one exception, and they appear only inside prose.

rules.name: The Weight Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Chrome stops at 500. Weight 700 belongs only to Markdown `strong`.

rules.name: The Annotation Prefix Rule
rules.body: Empty or missing values are written as `#` comments in `ink-3` (`# none`, `# undated`, `# no summary`, `# nothing published yet`, `# no sheet matches "…"`). A blank space or an invented value is never used instead.

rules.name: The Rails Rule
rules.body: Rules run the full width of the window, and content never leaves the rails. Nothing is placed in the margins outside the column except the rules' own run-out, the `table`, and the hatch band beside each rail.

rules.name: The Registration Rule
rules.body: A registration cross (11px, two 1px `ink-3` strokes) is centred on every point where a full-width rule crosses a rail, and nowhere else. A row with no rule of its own carries no crosses.

rules.name: The Marked-Not-Lifted Rule
rules.body: A surface is never lifted. The sheet under the pointer or focus is marked at its corners and tinted, and nothing about it rises, casts a shadow, or gains a heavier edge.

dos: **Do** set everything in Fira Code with ligatures off on a 16px base, and measure horizontal insets in `ch`.
**Do** open every surface with the labelled hairline nav rule as the drawing's first full-width rule, `──┼─ docs.osm.sh ──── osm.sh │ puzzles ─┼──`.

**Do** build every surface as one ruled drawing: a column of at most 76rem between full-height `rule` rails, rows cut by full-width `rule` hairlines, and an 11px `ink-3` registration cross wherever a rule crosses a rail.
**Do** let cells share their edges. Each cell draws only its right and bottom, so no line is ever doubled.
**Do** mark the sheet in hand with four `rose-ink` corner crosses and a 60% `ground-2` tint.
**Do** lay the drawing on the `table`, with the 28px hatch band beside each rail and a construction grid on the 16px unit in every title block's lettering cell.
**Do** keep search first: the find row sits directly under the title block, `/` reaches it from anywhere, and matches are redlined in `rose-wash` over a `rose` underline.
**Do** set every page as one numbered sheet (`001`, counting up from the oldest) in a single set, newest first.
**Do** write missing values as `#` comments in `ink-3` (`# none`, `# undated`, `# no summary`, `# nothing published yet`) and keep counts true (`0 sheets`).
**Do** keep motion to the redline sweep (180ms), the find stroke (200ms), and colour, tint, and mark fades (150ms), all on `--ease-out-expo`, and honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** theme the browser: `rose` selection, `rose-ink` caret and focus ring, a thin `rule` scrollbar on a `ground-2` track, `color-scheme: light`, and `theme-color` set to the ground.
donts: **Don't** distinguish article kinds on the index with tabs, badges, colour, or grouping. Kinds live only in directories and URL segments.

**Don't** put a second surface or a texture inside the column beyond the title block's construction grid. That rules out a gridded mat, cards, panels, and noise or grain anywhere. Texture is drafting linework: the margin hatch and the construction grid.
**Don't** knock the hatch out behind a mark. A paper patch under a registration cross breaks the rail it sits on.
**Don't** draw a line in any colour but `rule`, or heavier than 1px. Show emphasis with a mark, never by darkening a line.
**Don't** introduce a second typeface or a chrome weight above 500.

**Don't** add a drop shadow or blur, or use a gradient as a tonal fill. Gradients in this system only draw hard-stop lines (the registration crosses, the sheet marks, the ruler ticks, the margin hatch, the construction grid) or a flat wash (the redline).
**Don't** put rose anywhere but a redline, a focus mark, the marks on the sheet in hand, a hovered link, or the selection.

**Don't** turn the index into a dashboard or a marketing hero (stat tiles, featured heroes, tag clouds), or into an app shell with a sidebar of sections. The title block's fields are the only figures.
**Don't** ship a dark theme. This is a whiteprint in daylight.
**Don't** invent sheets, dates, summaries, or counts to fill an empty grid.
